text:
erin: quick drop 10m thread: i built an exposure matrix for untangling cross-cutting dependencies. goal: surface minimal cut points where a small change dramatically reduces blast radius. spreadsheet + viz: https://redwood.internal/notes/exposure-matrix-2026 :bar_chart:
kai: nice. can you paste the top 6 cut points you found? a short list helps devs prioritize.
erin: pasted top-6 cut points (rank, cut-point, impact):
1) tenant-routing -> shared-cache (impact: reduces p99 tail and deploy blast, est ROI 2.1x)
2) auth-check -> billing-core sync call (impact: most deploys hang on auth flake)
3) telemetry-ingest -> session-router ack path (impact: churn and retries)
4) model-proxy internal metrics shipping (impact: noisy telemetry inflates alerts)
5) quota-enricher sync enrich call from frontend (impact: increases cold-start latency)
6) shared-kv-store schema coupling (impact: prevents independent deploys)
mika: those map closely to things we see in the incident heatmap. proposal: pick top-3 cut points for a pilot: tenant-routing, auth->billing, shared-kv schema. each gets a 3-6 month runway with owner+steward.
samir: nit: how are you estimating ROI? we need simple signals: reduced deploy-failures, mean time to recovery, and p99 improvement. also add maintenance-hours-saved so PMs can sign off.
erin: ROI calc is in the sheet (very rough): baseline incidents * avg cost per incident + dev-hours saved from fewer rollbacks -> projected yearly savings. i'll export a small slice for the pilot that shows expected delta.
kai: for tenant-routing cut: recommend a two-pronged approach: (A) extract a tiny routing facade that owns tenant resolution and TTL caching, (B) swap consumers progressively via header-based routing. facade should be stateless and run in cheaper infra if possible.
mika: add a compatibility shim that returns X-Routing-Source header so we can measure adoption. also synthetic tests to ensure routing parity across tenant sets.
samir: for auth->billing: critical path. suggest an async auth-validation token: callers get a short-lived token after async validation; billing-core validates token rather than doing sync auth checks. reduces tail and decouples lifecycle.
